correctness.rationale: Every unit has nonzero diagonal coordinates and arbitrary independent radical arrow coordinates. For each arrow, a single linear equation in two radical coordinates has q^2 solutions exactly when the paired torus colors agree, and q otherwise; summing its product over vertex colorings proves the FK evaluation for every finite quiver and field. Burnside gives the exact class count. For triangular orientations over F_p, unique normal Sylow p-subgroup identifies a semisimple torus module and its full character relations: cyclic (t,t,t) versus transitive (t,t,-t), distinct under any coordinate permutation for p>=5. Explicit finite brute-force multiplication checks support, but do not replace, proof; infinite quantifiers are addressed symbolically.

value.rationale: Complete exact conjugacy-class and commuting-probability enumerations for every finite quiver, all finite fields and loops/multiple arrows connect a structural group invariant to the standard FK polynomial. The full orientation invariance is substantive because an explicit infinite family of nonisomorphic groups has the same invariants. The construction exposes specific information loss, not merely a reparameterization of a single numerical case. The nearest ring-element adjoint-rank work does not answer the unit-group class-count/isomorphism question.
